quotes.text: But the real failure is role confusion. One agent trying to plan a change, call Graph, write a remediation script, request approval, verify the result and document it is like running a help desk, a change board, and a post-mortem with one very tired intern.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains crisply why a single do-everything agent fails in enterprise workflows.

quotes.text: The planner focuses on intent and constraints. The operator focuses on tools and execution. The reviewer focuses on guardrails, approvals and are we grounded in facts? Each agent keeps a clean short instruction set with the minimum memory it needs.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines the core planner-operator-reviewer role split of a multi-agent system.

quotes.text: The operator doesn't approve their own change. The analyst doesn't mess with production. The QA doesn't write the code they're approving, simple, boring, safe.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures separation of duties as the safety principle behind agent roles.

quotes.text: Document your policies as data: mutual exclusivity rules, license bundles, device baselines. Put them in structured form. Models can select, they shouldn't invent.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete, reusable rule for keeping agent decisions bounded.

quotes.text: If you remember one thing: single agents help, but teams of agents, planned, tool driven and permission scoped, quietly transform your environment while you pretend to sleep.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarises the episode's central recommendation in one sentence.

chapters.title: Why multi-agent systems get work done
The limits of a single agent
Multi-agent roles, tools and safety boundaries
Building with Azure AI Foundry and Semantic Kernel

takeaways: Splitting work across planner, operator and reviewer agents reduces role confusion, hallucinations and risky changes compared with one do-everything agent.
Azure AI Foundry provides agent definitions, models, knowledge, tools, content safety and tracing, while Semantic Kernel orchestrates the agent loop in code.
Every agent needs its own managed identity with least privilege, PIM-gated destructive actions, human approvals and full tracing in Log Analytics.
hook: Single AI agents that try to plan, execute, approve and document everything stall or break things in production. This episode shows Microsoft 365 and Azure admins how to build a governed multi-agent system with Azure AI Foundry and Semantic Kernel that safely automates Intune, Entra and Graph tasks.
